title: I’ve been experimenting with dragon flight in Unreal Engine
author: No-Blacksmith7127

comments.author: dustandwater
comments.body:
This looks fantastic. It could be on the verge of being a full game already.

Yes, it feels like it would fit perfectly as a traversal mechanic in a massive RPG like Skyrim, but it also could just be what you’ve shown here.

Either some sort of racing game, or a destruction type of game where you fly around terrorising villages. The villagers put up more defences over time, and you have to break through them.

The flight itself looks good. It feels physical. The wings seem consequential: when they flap, the flight responds. It’s really impressive.

comments.author: liright
comments.body: Legitimately what do you think is difficult about what OP showed? The environment is super basic and mostly done with pre-existing assets from the UE store. There is also no "game" at all, it's basically just the flying of the dragon and hurling fire, that's it. The only impressive part about it all is the dragon 3D model + animations, the fluidity and the camera effects. If I gave Opus 5.5 ultracode a few hours I bet it could create a similar dragon model along with rigging, then it's all about iteration in the animations and fludity. I am doing the same with my game about the car behavior, fluidity of animations and transititions between them, suspension movement etc and I know AI is absolutely capable of that because I've seen it, I have not written a single line of code or designed a single model.

replies.author: trai1er_dude
replies.body:
I've never seen that environment on fab and i've been using fab (ue marketplace before) for like 8 years and have 1000s of assets. Creating an environment like that is not a quick process and once again shows your complete lack of knowledge.

I'm pretty sure you couldn't get a dragon model that good via any non specialized LLM currently. With specialized tools like Meshy/Tripo/Rodin it can be done but then getting it to be rigged in a decent way can be difficult. The real difficulty comes with animations and all that comes with that, there is currently no good way for one AI tool to do complex animations for non humanoid creatures especially complex creatures like dragons, i've actually looked into this for my own projects and the current one stop AI tools are not good. Admittedly there are some workflows combining many tools like ai video generation and using blender mcp but it's not a quick solution and results aren't always great.

The real complexity here outside getting/creating those animations is setting up the character controller in a way which looks this good with the animation blending, physical animations, animation states and all the logic behind that, that is an extremely tough thing to do well and takes weeks/months of tuning, i have experience with non humanoid models which are less complex than this and they can take months to fine tune to get movement looking and feeling just right.

On top of all that there's just the general level of polish which can be seen with the animations, lighting, transitions, vfx, level design, performance, overall creature and camera movement etc etc etc.

You've said yourself you have no idea about game dev so stop wasting both our time, as some one who has been building games for a long time with and without AI i can tell you for a fact this would not be an easy thing to recreate hence why it's got this level of attention and why most the games on this sub are so basic by comparison. If it was so easy to do you'd see a ton of people with games like this.
